item.title: Equality of the Jellium and the Uniform Electron Gas Energies
item.description: arXiv:2610.20910v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Jellium, a system of electrons in a uniform neutralizing background, and the uniform electron gas (UEG), a system of electrons with constant density and no background, are two standard models of the electron gas. We prove that the ground-state energy per unit volume of Jellium, as defined by Lieb and Narnhofer, coincides with the UEG energy defined by Lewin, Lieb and Seiringer, i.e. \[ e^\hbar_{\rm Jel}(\rho_0)=e^\hbar_{\rm UEG}(\rho_0). \] This equality was previously established in the classical case by Lewin, Lieb and Seiringer and independently by Cotar and Petrache.
item.dc:creator: Mih\'aly A. Csirik

item.title: Free Fermion frustration-free models have zero Hall conductance
item.description: arXiv:2610.21172v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We give a new proof that translation-invariant free Fermion frustration-free models have zero Hall conductance. Our proof is analytic in nature and it uses the bulk-edge correspondence. The central argument, which holds beyond the translation-invariant situation, is that in frustration-free models, edge modes cannot merge into the ground state band. We give an example of a gapped frustration-free model that is nonetheless gapless on the half-plane.
item.dc:creator: Sven Bachmann, Zhiqian Du, Martin Fraas

item.title: Poisson statistics for one-dimensional Anderson--Bernoulli Schr\"odinger operators
item.description: arXiv:2610.21268v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We prove Poisson local eigenvalue statistics for one-dimensional Schr\"odinger operators with nondegenerate Bernoulli potentials at any fixed nonzero coupling. After unfolding by the integrated density of states (IDS), the local eigenvalue process converges to a Poisson point process of unit intensity at every energy in the interior of the almost-sure spectrum. The theorem also holds for bounded nonconstant iid potentials, provided the IDS is continuous and strictly increasing near the reference energy. If the IDS also has a finite positive derivative at that energy, the usual linear normalization gives the same limit. The proof uses a phase coordinate with exact IDS drift to obtain a uniform exponential crossing law and joint Poisson counts in disjoint energy windows.
item.dc:creator: Yi Han

item.title: Semiclassical Band Splitting in the Infinite Chern Band Model
item.description: arXiv:2610.21462v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study the two lowest Bloch bands of the infinite Chern band model in the semiclassical limit. When the Berry curvature parameter is an odd multiple of \(\pi\), we derive an explicit asymptotic formula for their exponentially small splitting, uniformly over the Brillouin torus. The proof combines Agmon estimates and WKB approximations for a matrix Schr\"odinger operator whose lowest potential eigenvalue has two wells. Geometric properties of the Agmon distance allow us to compute the leading tunneling coefficients by the method of stationary phase. We provide numerical computations to illustrate the asymptotic formula and support the conjecture that the two bands remain separated for other values of the Berry curvature parameter.
item.dc:creator: Tyler Guo

item.title: Approach to Equilibrium in Translation-Invariant Quantum Systems: Structural Results II
item.description: arXiv:2610.21475v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We continue the development, started in [AHP 25 (2023), 715-749], of a structural theory of approach to equilibrium in translation-invariant quantum spin systems. Dynamical Steady States (DSS) are defined as w*-limit points of the time-averaged evolution of an initial state. We show that if a DSS is an equilibrium state of a sufficiently regular interaction, then the specific energy of this interaction is necessarily a constant of the motion. Two distinct mechanisms lead to this conclusion, one based on dynamical surface energies and the other on conservation of specific relative entropy. We conjecture that these properties hold for a natural class of interactions. For a DSS admitting a physical equilibrium description, the associated equilibrium states are characterized by a dynamical Gibbs variational principle: they are precisely the minimizers of the specific relative entropy from the initial state over the physical equilibrium states. The achieved minimum equals the increase of specific entropy. The structural theory also yields characterizations of approach to thermal equilibrium, based on two model-dependent questions: restoration of a sufficiently local thermodynamic description at large times and classification of the corresponding local constants of motion. Once locality is restored, the constants of motion determine the possible asymptotic equilibrium states. In particular, if finite-range locality is restored and the energy is the only finite-range constant of the motion, then every DSS is a thermal equilibrium state at the temperature fixed by energy conservation. The finite-time dynamical input underlying this theory is established in a companion paper.
item.dc:creator: Vojkan Jak\v{s}i\'c, Claude-Alain Pillet, Anna Szczepanek

item.title: Dynamical Conservation Laws in Quantum Spin Systems
item.description: arXiv:2610.21489v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study dynamical conservation laws and the propagation of thermodynamic structure in translation-invariant lattice quantum spin systems. Using Lieb-Robinson bounds [CMP 28 (1972), 251-257] in arbitrary dimension, and Araki's bounds [CMP 14 (1969), 120-157] in dimension one, we prove conservation of the specific entropy, specific energy, and specific relative entropy under suitable assumptions on the interactions. The transported local Hamiltonians admit surface energies that vanish per unit volume in the van Hove limit, and local observables remain a core for the transported generators at every finite time. Weak Gibbsianity is preserved for sufficiently small times in arbitrary dimension and for all times in dimension one. These results provide the analytical foundation for the structural theory of approach to equilibrium developed in a companion paper, and establish partial results toward the conjectures formulated there.
item.dc:creator: Vojkan Jak\v{s}i\'c, Claude-Alain Pillet, Anna Szczepanek

item.title: Augmentation curve for torus knots
item.description: arXiv:2610.21585v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We prove a version of topological recursion for the correlation differentials of colored HOMFLY-PT polynomials of torus knots on the corresponding augmentation curves, following the proposal of Gu, Jockers, Klemm, and Soroush. To this end, we explicitly construct the spectral curve from the so-called auxiliary curve of Brini, Eynard, and Mari\~no and prove that it coincides with the augmentation curve for every torus knot with coprime $(r,s)$. Finally, our version of topological recursion proves the higher-genus closed-string prediction of the Aganagic--Vafa conjecture for all torus knot augmentation curves.
item.dc:creator: Alexander Hock, Sergey Shadrin

item.title: On the exact quantization of BCOV Theory on Calabi-Yau Manifolds
item.description: arXiv:2610.21927v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We announce the solution of constructing perturbative quantum BCOV invariants on arbitrary Calabi-Yau manifolds. In this note, we outline the construction and present an explicit solution. The quantization includes all descendant fields and all loop orders, and expresses the quantum BCOV interaction by an explicit integration over the moduli space of marked Riemann surfaces. This canonical solution provides a mathematical construction of all higher genus BCOV invariants on compact Calabi-Yau manifolds, which are conjecturally equivalent to all higher genus Gromov-Witten invariants on the mirror.
item.dc:creator: Si Li, Minghao Wang

item.title: Fixed-Point Abundances and the Onset of Extinctions in Multispecies Lotka-Volterra Ecosystems
item.description: arXiv:2610.22183v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: I investigate the average and variance of species abundance distributions for fixed-point solutions to generalized Lotka-Volterra ecosystems. Two different analytical methods are constructed. First, I build up on the perturbative Random Matrix Theory approach developed in my earlier work [Phys. Rev. E. 113, L062202 (2026)], and formalize this method diagrammatically. The abundance average is given by a sum of planar diagrams with non-crossing vertex pairings which can be encoded as Dyck paths. This allows me to express the combinatorial factor multiplying perturbative terms at each order as Catalan and Narayana numbers, following which the abundance average is given by the latter's generating functions. In this way, the infinite perturbation expansion is exactly resummed in a closed-form formula. I have not been able to find a similar resummation for the abundance variance, however diagrammatic Feynman rules are expressed, following which the perturbative series can be calculated to any desirable order. Second, I do the same calculations using the cavity method, which gives closed-form formulas for both the abundance average and variance. For the average, the cavity formula gives the exact same result as the perturbative approach when the average interspecies interaction vanishes. When this is not the case, the two results are functionally different, however they are hardly distinguishable in their parametric range of validity. Comparison with numerical data indicate that the cavity result is more accurate over a larger parameter range.
item.dc:creator: Philippe Jacquod

item.title: The \textsc{ABC}-equation revisited: missed integrable cases. Part I: classification and (quasi) integrable structures
item.description: arXiv:2610.20672v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We consider the \textsc{ABC}-equation $Au_xu_{yt} + Bu_yu_{xt} + Cu_tu_{xy} = 0$, $A$, $B$, $C\in\mathbb{R}$, which was proved to be integrable in the case $A + B + C = 0$ (the Veronese web equation). Our study reveals ten more cases that admit integrable structures that, to the best of our knowledge, where not known before. The techniques is based essentially on the theory of the tangent and cotangent coverings.
item.dc:creator: I. S. Krasil'shchik

item.title: Region bounds, error margins and certified positivity in the numerical conformal bootstrap; Or the first mathematically rigorous bounds on the 3d Ising CFT critical exponents
item.description: arXiv:2610.20701v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Numerical conformal bootstrap bounds are commonly called rigorous, yet as published they are not theorems: they hold at sampled points rather than on regions of parameter space, for truncated rational approximations of the conformal blocks, for a finite list of spins, and up to floating-point rounding. We close all four gaps. We show how to search efficiently for functionals positive on regions, including external-dimension space; how positivity on the large-spin crossing vectors can be imposed as such a region constraint; how new analytic bounds on the conformal-block recursion relations give functionals positive on the true, untruncated crossing vectors; and how to certify the positivity of these functionals in exact arithmetic. The certification rests on Bernstein-basis positivity certificates in up to three variables, exact arithmetic in $\mathbb{Q}(\sqrt2)$, a compactified treatment of the infinite spin tail, and an explicit bound on the difference between the true blocks and their truncations, so that infinitely many positivity conditions reduce to finitely many machine-checked sign conditions. As a flagship application we certify an exclusion region in the $(\Delta_\sigma,\Delta_\epsilon)$ plane: for $\Delta_\sigma\in[0.505,0.5405]$ all of $\Delta_\epsilon\in(1/2,3]$ is excluded except a small rectangle containing the 3d Ising island, giving rigorous two-sided bounds on the critical exponents $\eta$ and $\nu$ under explicitly stated spectrum assumptions. The analytic inputs for the mixed $\sigma$-$\epsilon$ system, which would remove the spin-2 gap assumption, are also proved. The same methods prevent common practical failure modes and can make bootstrap searches faster: region bounds turn the mapping of an island into a handful of one-dimensional bisections. The essential code to reproduce the search and the certification, and all machine-checkable certificates, are released.
item.dc:creator: Marten Reehorst

item.title: Infinite magic and the emergence of the continuum
item.description: arXiv:2610.20790v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Which features of a quantum state are needed for a relativistic quantum field theory to emerge from a lattice system? We address this question by establishing a quantitative relationship between the type classification of hyperfinite von Neumann algebras and the quantum-information-theoretic resource of nonstabilizerness, also called magic. Our results establish two complementary parts of this relationship. First, we prove that any stabilizer system on a lattice defines a canonical GNS Hilbert space in which local von Neumann algebras do not contain type III factors in their central decomposition. As an explicit example, we prove that for stabilizer systems with short-range order, the local algebras are isomorphic to tensor products of hyperfinite factors of type I or type II. This demonstrates that the absence of magic is accompanied by the absence of type III factors in the local algebras, therefore prohibiting the appearance of a quantum field theory. Second, for the hyperfinite factors of Araki, Woods and Powers, we prove a quantitative equivalence: The limiting factor is of type III if and only if the locally optimized min-relative entropy of magic diverges. This divergence is necessary to generate the continuous spectrum associated to a type III factor. Thus, in this setting, the emergence of a type III factor requires not merely the presence of magic, but an infinite amount of it. These results provide a rigorous setting supporting the proposal that infinite magic is a necessary structural ingredient for the emergence of a relativistic continuum from lattice systems.
item.dc:creator: Leo Shaposhnik, Lorenzo Leone, Lennart Bittel, Dimitris Saraidaris, Alexander Jahn, Jens Eisert

item.title: Radiation Conditions and Uniqueness Theorems for Open Wave-guide Networks
item.description: arXiv:2610.20891v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We state radiation conditions and prove a variety of uniqueness theorem for models of wave-guide networks, including acoustic wave-guide networks, and electromagnetic wave-guide networks described by the time harmonic Maxwell equations. To analyze Maxwell wave-guide networks we need to establish generalizations of the Mourre estimates from [29, 32].
item.dc:creator: Charles L. Epstein, Rafe Mazzeo, Solomon Quinn, Andras Vasy

item.title: A Coupled Fluid Naghdi Shell Windkessel Model for Pulmonary Artery Banding: Partitioned Numerical Scheme and Parameter Estimation
item.description: arXiv:2610.20966v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We develop a 3D fluid structure interaction model for blood flow through deformable vessels with localized constrictions, motivated by pulmonary artery banding in neonates with congenital heart disease. The model couples incompressible Navier Stokes equations in an Arbitrary Lagrangian Eulerian framework with a Naghdi shell model for the arterial wall and a three element Windkessel model for downstream circulation. The shell describes a 3D cylindrical vessel wall with variable radius and is defined on a 2D reference domain. Its low regularity formulation retains membrane, bending, and transverse shear deformation while requiring only first derivatives of the reference midsurface, accommodating piecewise smooth geometries with discontinuous surface slopes. We derive the coupled variational formulation and develop a non-iterative partitioned scheme with a Robin-type interface condition incorporating arterial wall inertia. For a linearized fixed domain problem, we establish a discrete energy estimate under suitable assumptions. A unscented Kalman filter estimates proximal and distal resistances and compliance from inlet-pressure observations. Numerical experiments demonstrate consistent pressure wave propagation and wall deformation under spatial and temporal refinement. Comparisons of the standard Naghdi shell and a modified, predominantly radial shell model reveal how structural deformation mechanisms affect wave speed and displacement. An idealized pulmonary artery banding example demonstrates the coupled fluid shell Windkessel model with parameter estimation. The framework enables investigation of the hemodynamic and mechanical effects of localized constrictions and their dependence on downstream vascular properties.
item.dc:creator: Yifan Wang, Josip Tambaca, Suncica Canic

item.title: Statistical Mechanics of Spike Trains: Self-Consistent Activity Ensembles and Phase Transitions
item.description: arXiv:2610.20971v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We introduce a statistical-mechanical framework for spiking neuronal systems in which entire spike trains, defined as spatiotemporal configurations of discrete events, are treated as microstates of the system. Instead of modeling explicit network dynamics, we construct an ensemble over complete spike histories and assign to each configuration an effective energy functional that quantifies its consistency with intrinsic synaptic interactions. This formulation leads to a Boltzmann-like distribution over spike configurations, where an effective temperature captures the influence of external inputs acting as a stochastic drive. Macroscopic states are described in terms of coarse-grained observables, such as population firing-rate densities, and arise from a competition between energetic contributions favoring interaction-consistent spike patterns and entropic contributions favoring spatio-temporal disorder. Within this framework, we primarily characterize the transition between oscillatory and non-oscillatory activity. The non-oscillatory regime contains both broadly distributed, approximately uniform states and temporally localized collapsed states, whereas the oscillatory regime is characterized by repeated activity peaks. These regimes are diagnosed using order parameters derived from the population spike-rate density, including its entropy, temporal localization measures, and autocorrelation-based indicators. To complement the analytical treatment, we perform Monte Carlo simulations that sample the ensemble of admissible spike configurations using a Metropolis-Hastings scheme defined directly on spike trains. The simulations reveal the emergence of the predicted macroscopic regimes and provide a direct sampling-based probe of the free-energy landscape.
item.dc:creator: Jan Pyrzowski, Laura Messio, Guillaume Marrelec, Marcin Markiewicz

item.title: Singular wave functions and quantum collapse in inverse-power potentials
item.description: arXiv:2610.21044v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Quantum collapse (QC) occurs under the action of the inverse-power potential U(r)=-U_{0}/(2r^{n}) in the framework of the Schroedinger equation. The corresponding stationary wave functions feature an infinite number of spatial oscillations at $r\rightarrow 0$. The ground state (GS) is missing in the presence of the QC, but the available bound states at finite energies may be physically relevant, as they are normalizable. This work aims to produce singular stationary wave functions. The analytical findings represent an asymptotic form of the stationary wave functions at $r\rightarrow 0$, which fill a continuous spectrum, and some exact solutions for the wave functions, obtained under appropriate conditions. As a regularized version, we also consider the potential truncated at a finite difference from the center. The regularized wave functions feature a finite number of spatial oscillations, the missing GS reappears, and the spectrum of the bound states is discrete.
item.dc:creator: Hidetsugu Sakaguchi, Boris Malomed

item.title: Formation of Trapped Surfaces for the Einstein-Euler System
item.description: arXiv:2610.21124v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We prove the formation of trapped surfaces for the Einstein--Euler system in 3+1 dimensions beyond spherical symmetry. We consider smooth characteristic initial data in a short-pulse regime with rapid fluid injection. Starting from initial data containing no trapped surfaces, we obtain two sufficient criteria for trapped surface formation, corresponding to the shear and fluid contributions, respectively. In particular, for the fluid-driven criterion, we impose no positive lower bound on the shear flux. To handle the multiple propagation speeds associated with gravitational waves, sound waves, and fluid transport, our analysis combines three ingredients: a coercive fluid energy current whose null fluxes reflect the unequal velocity components, curvature renormalizations adapted to the matter terms, and weighted geometric estimates controlling derivatives in all spacetime directions. To ensure that fluid injection alone can lead to trapped surface formation, we use particle-number conservation in a designed spacetime region to control the focusing process and obtain the desired sphere-integrated fluxes.
item.dc:creator: Xinliang An, Sifan Yu

item.title: Asymptotics of the Moduli Spaces of Parabolic $\mathrm{SL}(3,\mathbb C)$-Higgs Bundles
item.description: arXiv:2610.21303v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We study the large-scale geometry of the moduli spaces of stable strongly parabolic $\mathrm{SL}(3,\C)$-Higgs bundles on the three-punctured sphere for a family of parabolic weights. We glue the local Toda model metric to a decoupled metric obtained from the spectral line bundle, and perturb the resulting approximate metrics to harmonic metrics adapted to the parabolic structure. We also prove that Hitchin's $L^2$ metric approaches the semi-flat metric exponentially. The metric comparison and the spectral period calculation show that each moduli space is a complete ALG gravitational instanton of type $E_6$. The asymptotic estimates are uniform on compact subintervals of the weight chamber.
item.dc:creator: Shiyu Cao

item.title: Anti-successors and anti-replicators, Manin products and Koszul duality
item.description: arXiv:2610.21365v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We develop an operadic theory of anti-splitting and anti-replication for binary operads. For a binary operad $\opd$, we define its anti-bisuccessor $\ABSu(\opd)$ and anti-trisuccessor $\ATSu(\opd)$, with the property that an operation of $\opd$ splits into a negative sum of two or three operations, yielding canonical operad morphisms $\opd \to\ABSu(\opd)$ and $\opd\to\ATSu(\opd)$. For binary quadratic operads, the process gives Manin black products, \[ \ABSu(\opd) \cong \antiprelie \bullet \opd, \qquad \ATSu(\opd)\cong \antipostlie\bullet\opd. \] Dually, we introduce the anti-duplicator \(\ADup(\mathcal P)\) and anti-triplicator \(\ATrip(\mathcal P)\) and prove \[ \ADup(\opd^!)\cong \ABSu(\opd)^!, \qquad \ATrip(\opd^!)\cong \ATSu(\opd)^!. \] Consequently, the anti-duplicator gives a new way to calculate Manin white products. %, in particular, $\ADup(\opd)\cong \antiperm\circ\opd$. The framework recovers known anti-splittings, including anti-dendriform, anti-pre-Lie, and anti-pre-Poisson structures, in a uniform operadic form and produces further examples and dual pairs.
item.dc:creator: Chengming Bai, Li Guo, Yunhe Sheng, You Wang

item.title: Half-space last passage percolation with inhomogeneous first row
item.description: arXiv:2610.21413v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We consider exponential last passage percolation in half-space with a deterministic first row. This model corresponds to a version of TASEP in half-space in which particles enter at the origin and are restricted by a moving wall. We determine the possible limiting distributions of rescaled last passage times depending on the boundary strength and the choice of the wall. As key inputs to our analysis, we establish several results for point-to-point half-space last passage times, including upper tail bounds, weak convergence, and bounds on the probabilities that geodesics touch the diagonal for certain start and end points.
item.dc:creator: Patrik L. Ferrari, Sabrina Gernholt

item.title: Strict unimodality of the exact time-domain diffuse-light response under a Robin boundary condition
item.description: arXiv:2610.21431v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Time-domain boundary measurements of diffuse light are temporal point-spread functions whose peak position is used as a robust scalar datum in diffuse optical and fluorescence imaging. We consider the exact response generated by a single fluorescent point target in a homogeneous half-space with a Robin boundary condition. The response is a temporal convolution of two diffusion Green-function factors containing a complementary-error-function boundary correction. For every positive diffusion, absorption, depth, and source--target and detector--target distance parameter, and for every nonnegative Robin parameter, we prove that the normalized exact response is a generalized gamma convolution density. Its extension by zero to the negative half-line is bell-shaped. A differentiable small-time expansion, established by sectorial analyticity and Cauchy estimates, together with the sign-change structure of the first two derivatives, excludes tangential critical points and yields a unique peak with strict increase before it and strict decrease after it. The argument is exact and requires no large-distance, source--detector balance, symmetry, restricted-time, or small-parameter assumption. The same conclusion holds after convolution with an exponential fluorescence-lifetime density for every positive lifetime. The key ingredients are an explicit Stieltjes representation of the Robin factor, hyperbolic complete monotonicity, closure of the generalized gamma convolution class, and bell-shape theory. A derivation of the exact half-space model and the differentiated endpoint asymptotics are included in two appendices.
item.dc:creator: Junyong Eom, Jinwan Park

item.title: Difference between pair creation and anomaly matching: Nontrivial aspects of invertible symmetries and defects in $SU(N)$ models
item.description: arXiv:2610.21478v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We study the connection between the $SU(N)_{K}$ Wess-Zumino-Witten (WZW) model and $SU(N)_{K'}$ WZW models, enforcing the unbroken $\mathbb{Z}_{N}$ symmetries. The fundamental underlying structures are the (half-)integer spin simple currents in the topological quantum field theories and anomaly matching conditions in conformal field theories. For the (half-)integer spin simple current condition of the folded models $SU(N)_{K}\boxtimes_{\mathbb{Z}_{N}} \overline{SU(N)_{K'}}$ or $SU(N)_{K}\boxtimes_{\mathbb{Z}_{N}} SU(N)_{K'}$, we obtain the generalized pairing condition $K= \pm R^{2}K' (\text{mod}.N)$ with $\text{gcd}(R,N)=1$. On the other hand, the anomaly matching condition results in the weaker condition $K= \pm RUK' (\text{mod}.N)$ with $\text{gcd}(R,N)=\text{gcd}(U,N)=1$. Surprisingly, the anomaly matching without the pairing condition results in the intrinsic mismatch of the preservation law of the $\mathbb{Z}_{N}$ defects and symmetries. The pairing condition canonically relates symmetries and defects, as in category theory, whereas it is unclear whether it can be a guiding principle in prohibiting the massless renormalization group flows.
item.dc:creator: Yoshiki Fukusumi, Shuma Nakashiba

item.title: Statistical Characterization of Erratic and Chaotic Processes through Their Extrema I. Thermodynamics
item.description: arXiv:2610.21620v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We propose a general statistical framework for characterizing erratic functions through the statistics of their extrema, with the aim of identifying statistical signatures associated with chaotic processes. It is based on analyzing the extrema points of erratic functions associated with these processes. One is instructed to determine the probability distribution functions ( PDF)s of the locations of the extrema points, the spacings between the locations, in particular the nearest neighbors, and the ratios between adjacent spacings. We then fit these PDFs with PDFs known to relate to chaotic behavior like of random matrix theory. The extrema considered establish a cloud of points in general in $D$ dimensions for erratic function of several variables. For certain systems one finds also extrema curves. We further determine the ``thermodynamic" description of the erratic functions by computing the Shannon or differential entropy and by equating the PDFs to the Gibbs one. With this map we determine the ``energy function" and for certain cases also the ``temperature". We analyze three benchmark spacing PDFs: the Bernoulli shift map, the Poisson and the Gaussian beta ensemble and several others. We want to emphasize that the map to thermodynamics can be applied to variety of chaotic processes including non-physics ones. We distinguish marginal spacing distributions from joint distributions of consecutive spacings. The latter probe correlations and statistical organization that are invisible in one-spacing PDFs and may provide stronger signatures for distinguishing structured chaotic-like behavior from uncorrelated irregularity.
item.dc:creator: Jacob Sonnenschein

item.title: Degree Growth of Rational Maps with Laurent Property
item.description: arXiv:2610.21627v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Algebraic entropy measures the exponential growth of the degrees of iterates of rational self-maps. It is introduced by Bellon and Viallet in \cite{BellonandViallet}. We study degree growth for rational maps arising from recurrences with the Laurent property, with particular emphasis on Gale--Robinson recurrences. We develop a direct method for determining the degree growth from the recurrence relation itself, reducing the problem to the study of associated max-linear, or tropical recurrences. We first obtain a closed formula for the degrees of iterates for a broad class of homogeneous quadratic Laurent recurrences. We then apply this result to the two-term Gale--Robinson family and derive an explicit quadratic growth formula with a periodic correction term. For three-term Gale--Robinson recurrences, we express the algebraic entropy in terms of the associated tropical growth rate sequence. Based on explicit computations, we formulate a conjecture for the general three-term family predicting quadratic growth with a periodic correction. We prove the conjecture for the infinite family with parameters $p=1$, $q=2$, and $r\geq3$.
item.dc:creator: Melih Emin Can

item.title: Operator-Space Entanglement Entropy in Random Fermionic Gaussian Dynamics
item.description: arXiv:2610.21723v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We study the von Neumann operator-space entanglement entropy (OSEE) of initial product operators evolved under random gaussian dynamics, as modeled by a Brownian SYK$_2$ model. By exploiting a mapping to a domain-wall melting problem, we derive an exact expression for the time-dependent bipartite OSEE in the thermodynamic limit, and obtain an analytic characterization of the corresponding gaussian Page curve emerging at late times. Our results build on recent work on the entanglement dynamics in the all-to-all quantum simple exclusion process, leveraging tools from RMT, including the Coulomb-gas approach and a mapping to the free Jacobi process. Finally, based on our results, we discuss the possibility of relating the OSEE with non-gaussianity measures in the Heisenberg picture.
item.dc:creator: Pablo Bayona-Pena, Elena Gramellini, Lorenzo Piroli

item.title: Diffusion-Induced Stabilization of Nonreciprocal Wealth Dynamics
item.description: arXiv:2610.21861v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We study the stability of equal wealth shares in a spatial model combining local sharing, global redistribution, and random nonreciprocal interactions. On a two-dimensional square lattice in the infinite-system limit, the effect of local sharing depends on whether the influence of one site on another tends to have the same or opposite sign as the reverse influence. When these influences are nonnegatively correlated, diffusion reduces the redistribution required for stability, but a positive rate remains necessary. Negative correlations instead allow stability without redistribution, with the largest stability margin at finite diffusion and a return toward marginal stability at strong diffusion. This nonmonotonicity reflects a competition between spatial smoothing and the weakening of the stabilizing contribution of reciprocal anticorrelations. Equal shares can even remain stable under wealth-concentrating transfers, but only within an intermediate range of diffusion strengths.
item.dc:creator: Pierre Bousseyroux, Gilles Z\'erah, Michael Benzaquen

item.title: Vortex clusters and vortex-filled bubbles in a modified Abelian-Higgs model
item.description: arXiv:2610.21930v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We investigate a single-component Abelian-Higgs model with an eighth-order scalar potential whose vacuum manifold consists of two disconnected circles. The model supports two species of vortices and domain walls interpolating between the two vacuum components. We find type-1.5-like behavior characterized by nonmonotonic intervortex interactions and bound states of spatially separated vortices. Inner-vacuum vortices form clusters through short-range repulsion and long-range attraction, whereas outer-vacuum vortices form vortex-filled bubbles in which a closed domain wall confines multiple inner-vacuum-vortex cores. We construct the domain wall analytically, derive the asymptotic vortex-wall interactions, and analyze the fluctuation spectra of coincident multivortices to identify their splitting instabilities.
item.dc:creator: D. Migu\'elez-Caballero, S. Navarro-Obreg\'on, Muneto Nitta, Keisuke Ohashi

item.title: The derived category of a generalized complex torus
item.description: arXiv:2610.21960v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: For any translation invariant generalized complex structure J on a torus we construct the derived category D(J) generalizing the derived category of coherent sheaves on a complex torus and the affine/convergent Fukaya category of a symplectic torus. The category is defined in terms of a non-commutative curved deformation of the Dolbeault algebra of a complex torus. We show that this category is independent of the chosen deformation path, which we prove using non-commutative Fourier-Mukai duality. We also prove that the action of O(2n,2n; Z) on the space of generalized complex structures leaves the category D(J) invariant. In particular, T-duality acts trivially on D(J). We construct concrete objects associated to affine Lagrangians in the derived category associated to a symplectic torus and show that their spaces of morphisms are given by Floer cohomology. We show that our construction is consistent with the homological mirror symmetry conjecture (including its non-commutative version).
item.dc:creator: Patrick Antweiler, Vicente Cort\'es, Julian Holstein, Markus R\"oser, Aldo Witte

item.title: Classification of vanishing fusion rings of rank four
item.description: arXiv:2610.22000v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: A fusion ring is said to be vanishing if one of its multiplication matrices has determinant zero. We classify all vanishing fusion rings of rank four. We then provide a more explicit classification in the integral case, which allows us to derive several new consequences: there are infinitely many nonisomorphic simple integral vanishing fusion rings of rank four and no simple integral fusion ring of rank four is either $1$-Frobenius or Burnside.
item.dc:creator: Jingcheng Dong, S\'ebastien Palcoux, Arnaud Plessis

item.title: Nonpersistence of full-dimensional tori with polynomial decay in nonlinear Schr\"odinger equations
item.description: arXiv:2610.22072v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We establish local nonpersistence of full-dimensional invariant tori with polynomially decaying actions for the periodic quintic nonlinear Schr\"odinger equation \[ iu_t-u_{xx}+T_vu+\mu|u|^4u=0,\qquad x\in\mathbb T:=\mathbb R/(2\pi\mathbb Z). \] For every $\kappa\geq1$, we construct a fixed bounded real Fourier multiplier $T_ve^{ijx}=v_je^{ijx}$ whose frequencies $\lambda_j=j^2+v_j$ satisfy the Bourgain-type Diophantine condition \[ \operatorname{dist}\left(\sum_j\ell_j\lambda_j,\mathbb Z\right) \geq\gamma_\kappa\prod_j(1+\ell_j^2\langle j\rangle^{2\kappa})^{-1} \] for some $\gamma_\kappa>0$ and every nonzero finitely supported integer sequence $\ell$, where $\langle j\rangle=\max\{1,|j|\}$. For this multiplier, every $3<M<4\kappa+\frac12$, every $A>0$, and all sufficiently small $\mu A^2>0$, the closed relative action tube of radius $3/10$ around $I_j=A\langle j\rangle^{-M}$ contains no full-dimensional invariant torus in $H^1(\mathbb T)$ carrying a complete flow, with arbitrary frequencies allowed. This advances the study of the polynomial-decay problem identified by Kuksin as a main open problem in KAM theory for one-dimensional Hamiltonian PDEs [Amer. Math. Soc. Transl. Ser. 2, 212 (2004), 237--258, Problem 7.1]. Bourgain discussed a related question for short-range Hamiltonian systems [Russian Math. Surveys 59 (2004), 231--246, Section 3]. The proof combines simultaneous Diophantine and weighted homological estimates, an exact common-phase transformation, and one normal-form step on four adjacent Fourier coordinates. Uniform phase rotation forces an action excursion, while overlapping parameter intervals cover all sufficiently small positive perturbations. The mechanism suggests applications to other Hamiltonian PDEs.
item.dc:creator: Zhicheng Tong, Yong Li

item.title: Segal's semigroup, Virasoro structure, and Ward identities in Compactified Imaginary Liouville Theory
item.description: arXiv:2610.22170v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Compactified Imaginary Liouville Theory (CILT for short) is a probabilistically constructed Conformal Field Theory (CFT), expected to have connections to minimal models, Coulomb gas integrals, and loop models. In this paper, we study the quantization of Segal's semigroup given by CILT. Each element $\mathbf T_f$ in the quantized semigroup corresponds to a conformal annulus: the unit disk $\mathbb D$ with $f(\mathbb D^\circ)$ removed, where $f:\mathbb D\to f(\mathbb D)\subset \mathbb D^\circ$ is a contracting biholomorphism. This semigroup encodes the local conformal structure of the CFT, in particular the Virasoro symmetry with central charge $<1$ for CILT. We first relate the quantized Segal's semigroup to Segal's amplitudes of annuli and recover the Virasoro generators $\mathbf L_n,\widetilde{\mathbf L}_n$ ($n\geq0$) of CILT as generators of this semigroup. Compared to the real Liouville CFT, the main difficulty here is the absence of positivity, which we address through estimates for the imaginary Gaussian Multiplicative Chaos and non-self-adjoint operators. Using Segal's gluing axiom as in the real case, we differentiate the amplitude and use conformal covariance to derive the Ward identities in terms of all Virasoro operators $\mathbf L_n,\widetilde{\mathbf L}_n$ ($n\in\mathbb Z$). We also outline the parallel theory for Boundary CILT (BCILT), concerning Segal's semigroup of semiannuli. These results provide essential tools for the conformal bootstrap program of (B)CILT, boundary BPZ equations, boundary structure constants, and the global construction of conformal blocks.
item.dc:creator: Yang Xiao, Yuxiao Xie

item.title: A quadratic ancestor inequality for spanning trees
item.description: arXiv:2610.22180v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We introduce a quadratic ancestor inequality for weighted spanning trees on finite undirected graphs and give two applications. First, for every finite $n$-vertex transitive graph, the expected distance in its uniform spanning tree (UST) between two independent uniform vertices is at least $\sqrt{n}-1$, resolving a conjecture in [Benjamini--Kozma, Comm. Math. Phys. 259 (2005), 257--286]. Second, we prove that the growth exponent of three-dimensional loop-erased random walk (LERW) is at least 3/2.
item.dc:creator: Gefei Cai

item.title: Classical Capacity of Single-Mode Bosonic Gaussian Channels
item.description: arXiv:2610.22308v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: The classical capacity of a noisy optical channel is the maximum rate at which information can be transmitted reliably, given a constraint on the mean input energy. For the ubiquitous bosonic Gaussian channels, which include standard models of loss and noise in fibre and free-space optical links, determining this rate requires addressing whether entanglement between channel uses or non-Gaussian signals can outperform Gaussian encodings. More precisely, the question is whether the energy-constrained Holevo information is additive across arbitrarily many channel uses and coincides with its Gaussian counterpart. We answer these fundamental questions in the affirmative for every single-mode bosonic Gaussian channel at every input energy. Namely, we prove that independently prepared Gaussian states with Gaussian-distributed random displacements achieve the capacity, including in the low-energy regime where squeezing the signals competes with encoding information in their displacement. Our proof connects an entanglement inequality to a sharp, additive lower bound on output entropy. We then characterise communication above capacity: under a strict total photon-number cutoff, the probability of correct decoding decreases exponentially with the number of channel uses, and we derive explicit bounds on the decay exponent. When only the mean photon number is constrained, a simple energy-rescaling formula determines exactly the entire asymptotic rate--error trade-off: the capacity at mean photon number $N$ and allowed average decoding error $\epsilon$ equals the vanishing-error capacity at mean photon number $N/(1-\epsilon)$. Together, these results identify the ultimate limits of classical communication for some of the most fundamental models of optical communication.
item.dc:creator: Gerardo Adesso, Ludovico Lami, Vittorio Giovannetti

item.title: Stratification of opers with apparent singularities and isomonodromic bubbling
item.description: arXiv:2610.22326v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: On a compact Riemann surface of genus $g \geq 2$, we study Simpson's stratification of the de Rham moduli space of rank-2 flat connections. Upon representing flat $\mathrm{SL}_2(\mathbb{C})$-connections by branched projective structures, or equivalently by opers with apparent singularities, the stratum containing a flat connection is determined by the minimal number of apparent singularities needed to represent it. We construct explicit holomorphic families in which two simple apparent singularities collide and disappear, so that the family crosses into a smaller stratum; this realizes Simpson's closure relation between strata near generic points. The analogous families of Higgs bundles are described by Baker--Akhiezer divisors on the spectral curve in which two points converge to a pair of points exchanged by the spectral involution. We show that, before the collision, the two apparent singularities are joined by twin paths bounding a bubble, so that these families arise from the isomonodromic bubbling surgery discussed by Calsamiglia, Deroin and Francaviglia.
item.dc:creator: Duong Dinh, Troy Figiel, Joerg Teschner

item.title: The Dry Ten Martini Problem at Criticality
item.description: arXiv:2112.06869v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We solve the dry ten martini problem (lean-verified this time) by showing that every labeled almost Mathieu gap is open for $\lambda\neq 0$ and every irrational frequency. In particular, we prove that the maximum logarithmic height of each labeled gap is non-decreasing in the coupling $\lambda$ and extend an initial open seed gap for each gap label $n$ from $\lambda\in(0,\lambda_{n})$ to all $\lambda> 0$. The non-decreasing property follows from restoring time-reversal symmetry to the almost Mathieu operator $H$ by pairing it with its magnetic inverse $\bar{H}$. This allows us to express the logarithmic coupling derivative of the maximal gap height as the expectation value of a non-negative operator, yielding the required monotonicity.
item.dc:creator: Dan S. Borgnia, Matthew Faust

item.title: Construction of Gross-Neveu model using Polchinski flow equation
item.description: arXiv:2403.18562v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We develop a new method for solving the renormalization group flow equation, also known as the Polchinski equation, by formulating it as a well-posed infinite-dimensional partial differential equation on a Banach space. This yields the first direct construction of a solution of this equation via a fixed point argument, circumventing the need for perturbative or expansion-based techniques employed in earlier work. Our approach leverages recent advances in noncommutative probability theory, particularly a scale decomposition of the free fermionic field in a filtered noncommutative probability space equipped with a suitable conditional expectation. As a key application, we construct the Gross-Neveu model, a fermionic, asymptotically free, and scaling-critical quantum field theory. We rigorously establish convergence of the Schwinger functions as the cutoff is removed, and construct a random field on the noncommutative probability space of the free theory whose moments coincide with the Schwinger functions. This provides the first explicit strong coupling between the free and interacting fields for a scaling-critical quantum field theory. The method is expected to apply broadly to other critical or subcritical quantum field theories formulated in terms of bounded fields, including fermionic models such as the symplectic fermion model, as well as certain bosonic theories like the sine-Gordon model.
item.dc:creator: Pawe{\l} Duch

item.title: Generalized Dirac Equation in Metric-Affine Spacetimes: Consistency, Effective Mass, and Spinor Curvature
item.description: arXiv:2506.23609v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We formulate a generalized Dirac equation in four-dimensional metric-affine spacetimes with curvature, torsion, and non-metricity. The spinor connection is expanded over the complete basis of the Clifford algebra $cl(1,3)$ and contains eight complex coupling constants. Requiring agreement between direct covariantization of the Dirac equation and variation of the corresponding symmetrized Lagrangian imposes eight real consistency conditions, reducing the number of independent real parameters from sixteen to eight. In the static isotropic symmetric teleparallel sector, formal Hermiticity of the Hamiltonian with respect to the curved-space Dirac inner product reproduces the corresponding restrictions on the non-metricity and coframe couplings. The coframe-dependent terms introduce scalar and pseudoscalar mass contributions that persist in Minkowski spacetime. For a single free Dirac field with constant coefficients, they yield one effective mass, $m_{\mathrm{eff}}=\sqrt{(m-4b_3)^2+16b_4^2}$, and a chiral phase removable by a constant chiral field redefinition. A nonzero effective mass is therefore possible even when the original mass parameter vanishes. We also derive the Clifford decomposition of the generalized spinor curvature and show that it can remain nonzero when affine curvature, torsion, and non-metricity all vanish. When $m=0$, the combination $b_3^2+b_4^2$ determines both the effective mass squared and the surviving spinor curvature, establishing an algebraic link between these contributions.
item.dc:creator: Muzaffer Adak, Ali Bagci, Caglar Pala, Ozcan Sert

item.title: A Functorial Theory of Defects in Abelian Chern-Simons Theory
item.description: arXiv:2609.21414v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Recent work has constructed Abelian Chern-Simons theories as categorical TQFTs, allowing us to naturally incorporate categorical defects and construct defect extensions of Abelian Chern-Simons TQFTs. We first identify the Turaev-Viro realizations of Abelian Chern-Simons theory in the center and doubled pointed modular cases, clarifying the distinction between single bulk realizations and canonical doubled ones. Then we obtain Turaev-Viro partition functions in terms of Reidemeister-torsion densities. Alternatively, the Alterfold construction supplies the associated topological boundaries, domain walls, and condensation sectors, establishing an explicit Alterfold/Chern-Simons dictionary. We show that the finite quadratic module is the invariant controlling the bulk theory, its topological symmetries, orientation-reversal invariance, and defects. We further show that multicomponent Abelian BF theory arises as the extended TQFT of an off-diagonal Abelian Chern-Simons theory, placing it naturally within the same extended framework. Finally, we demonstrate that recently proposed Abelian Chern-Simons dualities do not define a genuine TQFT duality. These results provide a concrete model for defects in Abelian topological orders and suggest a route toward the non-Abelian case.
item.dc:creator: Daniel Galviz

item.title: A GLSM realization of derived equivalence in $U(1) \times U(2)$ models
item.description: arXiv:2312.05740v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: This paper studies the derived equivalence between Calabi--Yau mixed branches using the B-brane hemisphere partition function in anomalous gauged linear sigma models (GLSMs). For a family of anomalous $U(2)$ GLSMs, we study the infrared behavior of B-branes under RG flow and the variation of FI parameters in the quantum K\"ahler moduli space. As characterized by the big and small window categories of the GLSM, the RG flow effect is analyzed according to the properties of their B-brane central charges as hemisphere partition functions. The result generalizes the band restriction rules in anomalous abelian GLSMs (Clingempeel--Floch--Romo) to some $U(2)$ models. As an application, we study a family of $U(1)\times U(k)$ models for $k=1,2$, which realize a Fano UV sigma model and two IR phases as mixed branches accompanied by local Calabi--Yau Higgs components. By applying the restriction rules, we establish new derived equivalences between Calabi--Yau varieties from these anomalous models.
item.dc:creator: Jirui Guo, Ban Lin, Hao Zou

item.title: Computing the center of a fusion category
item.description: arXiv:2406.13438v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We present an algorithm for explicitly computing the categorical (Drinfeld) center of a pivotal fusion category. Our approach is based on decomposing the images of simple objects under the induction functor from the category to its center. We have implemented this algorithm in a general-purpose software framework TensorCategories for tensor categories that we develop within the open-source computer algebra system OSCAR. We compute explicit models for the centers in form of the tuples $(X,\gamma)$ where $X$ is an object and $\gamma$ is a half-braiding. From these models we can compute the $F$-symbols and $R$-symbols. Using the data from the AnyonWiki, we were able to compute the center together with its $F$-symbols and $R$-symbols for all the 279 multiplicity-free fusion categories up to rank 5, and furthermore some chosen examples of rank 6, including the Haagerup subfactor (presented in a separate paper). Some of these centers yield new high-rank and not multiplicity-free examples of modular categories, e.g. rank 21 and multiplicity 2.
item.dc:creator: Fabian M\"aurer, Ulrich Thiel

item.title: A proof of Onsager's Conjecture for the SQG equation
item.description: arXiv:2407.02578v5 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We construct solutions to the SQG equation that fail to conserve the Hamiltonian while having the maximal allowable regularity for this property to hold. This result solves the generalized Onsager conjecture on the threshold regularity for Hamiltonian conservation for SQG. We also prove nonuniqueness for arbitrary smooth data and an h-principle result.
item.dc:creator: Philip Isett, Sam Looi

item.title: Dark Subspaces and Invariant Measures of Quantum Trajectories
item.description: arXiv:2409.18655v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Quantum trajectories are Markov processes describing the evolution of a quantum system subject to indirect measurements. They can be viewed as place dependent iterated function systems or the result of products of dependent and non identically distributed random matrices. In this article, we establish a complete classification of their invariant measures. The classification is done in two steps. First, we prove a Markov process on some linear subspaces called dark subspaces, defined in (Maassen, K\"ummerer 2006), admits a unique invariant measure. Second, we study the process inside the dark subspaces. Using a notion of minimal family of isometries from a reference space to dark subspaces, we prove a set of measures indexed by orbits of a unitary group is the set of ergodic measures of quantum trajectories.
item.dc:creator: Tristan Benoist, Cl\'ement Pellegrini, Anna Szczepanek

item.title: Minimum nonlinearity for pattern-forming Turing instability in a mathematical autocatalytic model
item.description: arXiv:2412.13783v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Pattern formation is ubiquitous in nature and the mechanism widely-accepted to underlay them is based on the Turing instability, predicted by Alan Turing decades ago. This is a non-trivial mechanism that involves nonlinear interaction terms between the different species involved and transport mechanisms. We present here a mathematical analysis aiming to explore the mathematical constraints that a reaction-diffusion dynamical model should comply in order to exhibit a Turing instability. The main conclusion limits the existence of this instability to nonlinearity degrees larger or equal to three.
item.dc:creator: Javier L\'opez-Pedrares, Marcos Su\'arez-V\'azquez, Juan P\'erez-Mercader, Alberto P. Mu\~nuzuri

item.title: On the dynamics of leapfrogging vortex rings
item.description: arXiv:2503.21604v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: The evolution of highly concentrated vorticity around rings in the three-dimensional axisymmetric Euler equations is studied in a regime for which the leapfrogging dynamics predicted by Helmholtz is expected to occur. We provide in this paper the first result deriving this phenomenon for a general class of initial data in the suitable regime. The singular interaction of rings requires significant improvements of weak and strong localization estimates obtained in prior works. Our method is based on the combination of a new variational argument and a recently introduced double iterative procedure.
item.dc:creator: Martin Donati, Lars Eric Hientzsch, Christophe Lacave, Evelyne Miot

item.title: Empirical Quantum Advantage in Constrained Optimization from Encoded Unitary Designs
item.description: arXiv:2511.14296v4 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We introduce the Constraint-Enhanced Quantum Approximate Optimization Algorithm (CE-QAOA), a shallow, constraint-aware ansatz that operates inside the one-hot product space [n]^m, where m is the number of blocks and each block is initialized in an n-qubit W_n state. We give an ancilla-free, depth-optimal encoder that prepares W_n using n-1 two-qubit rotations per block, and a two-local block-XY mixer that preserves the one-hot manifold and has a constant spectral gap on the one-excitation sector. At the level of expressivity, we establish per-block controllability, implying approximate universality per block. At the level of distributional behavior, we show that, after natural block and symbol permutation twirls, shallow CE-QAOA realizes an encoded unitary 1-design and supports approximate second-moment (2-design) behavior; combined with a Paley-Zygmund argument, this yields finite-shot anticoncentration guarantees. Algorithmically, we wrap constant-depth sampling with a deterministic feasibility checker to obtain a polynomial-time hybrid quantum-classical solver (PHQC) that returns the best observed feasible solution in O(S n^2) time, where S is a polynomial shot budget. We obtain two advantages. First, when CE-QAOA fixes r >= 1 locations different from the start city, we achieve a Theta(n^r) reduction in shot complexity even against a classical sampler that draws uniformly from the feasible set. Second, against a classical baseline restricted to raw bitstring sampling, we show an exp(Theta(n^2)) minimax separation. In noiseless circuit simulations of traveling salesman problem instances with n in {4,...,10} locations from the QOPTLib benchmark library, we recover the global optimum at depth p = 1 using polynomial shot budgets and coarse parameter grids defined by the problem size.
item.dc:creator: Chinonso Onah, Roman Firt, Kristel Michielsen

item.title: Derivation of the Boltzmann equation from hard-sphere dynamics (after Y. Deng, Z. Hani, and X. Ma)
item.description: arXiv:2602.04407v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Consider a microscopic system of $N$ hard spheres that are initially independent (modulo the exclusion condition on particle positions) and identically distributed in $\mathbb{R}^3$. When the number $N$ of particles goes to infinity and the diameter $\varepsilon$ of the particles goes to zero, and under the weak density assumption $N\varepsilon^2=1$, it has been known since the work of Lanford that the empirical measure for the particles converges to the solution of the Boltzmann equation in a short time interval. In particular, the particles remain dynamically independent, in this limit and in the short time interval where the correlations induced by their collisions remain under control. In a recent work, Y. Deng, Z. Hani and X. Ma successfully obtained the same convergence result in arbitrary large time; more precisely, the convergence result holds for any time interval on which the Boltzmann equation has a regular solution. In this note, we explain a few elements of their proof.
item.dc:creator: Thierry Bodineau, Isabelle Gallagher, Laure Saint-Raymond, Sergio Simonella

item.title: Contractivity of time-dependent driven-dissipative systems
item.description: arXiv:2602.16067v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Experimentally relevant quantum systems are frequently described by a time-dependent Lindblad master equation in which the dissipation due to interaction with an environment is fixed, but the experimenter has control over the Hamiltonian, which therefore can change with time. A fundamental question that is also of practical relevance is to determine when such systems invariably lose information about their initial state (are exponentially contractive independent of the Hamiltonian) or when the control can be used to prevent this loss of information to some degree. Here, we identify the necessary and sufficient criterion on the dissipator for Hamiltonian-invariant contractivity. If the dissipator does not fulfil this criterion, but by itself is exponentially contractive, we also establish exponential contractivity for sufficiently weak or slow drives and construct examples where strong or fast driving prevents exponential contraction.
item.dc:creator: Lasse H. Wolff, Daniel Malz, Rahul Trivedi

item.title: The bulk spectral gap is certifiable from above but uncomputable from below
item.description: arXiv:2606.03836v4 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Determining spectral gaps in the thermodynamic limit is a central challenge in quantum many-body physics. When a fixed boundary condition is imposed, this problem is undecidable: no algorithm, even with unlimited resources, can decide for every Hamiltonian whether it is gapped. Yet the thermodynamic limit is meant to capture the intrinsic properties of very large systems, which should not depend on how their boundaries are chosen. Here, we therefore consider the bulk spectral gap problem, which concerns only the intrinsic excitations of the infinite system, independently of any boundary. We first give a general algorithm producing a hierarchy of certified upper bounds on the bulk gap, arbitrarily tight at the cost of more computation. Second, we prove that the spectral gap problem remains undecidable in the bulk: no algorithm can decide whether the bulk gap is positive, already for translationally invariant nearest-neighbour chains of fixed local dimension. The bulk spectral gap is thus certifiable from above but uncomputable from below. More precisely, the bulk-gaplessness promise problem is RE-complete, exactly as hard as the halting problem. The same construction also shows that deciding whether an explicitly given state is a ground state of the infinite system is undecidable. Finally, we apply the upper-bounding algorithm to the spin-1/2 kagome Heisenberg antiferromagnet to produce the first nontrivial certified upper bounds on its bulk gap.
item.dc:creator: Xiangling Xu, Matthias Sch\"otz, Jie Wang, Victor Magron, Igor Klep, Omar Fawzi, Marc-Olivier Renou

item.title: Gram--Wishart--Stiefel formulation of the $N=2$, large--$d$ gauge theory in 1D: towards emergent Grassmannian geometry
item.description: arXiv:2607.08481v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We develop the Gram/Wishart/Stiefel formulation of the \(N=2\), large--\(d\) planar endpoint theory of lattice BFSS/BMN matrix quantum mechanics on the lattice. The endpoint variables become rank--two Wishart eigenvalues and relative Stiefel angles, expressing the holonomy invariants \(A\), \(B\), and \(R^2=A^2+B^2\) in radial and angular Gram data. The large-\(R\) aligned contribution \(-A\) is absorbed into the Gaussian sector, producing the shifted mass \((\alpha_\Lambda)_{\rm eff}=\alpha_\Lambda-1/2\). The exact \(O(2)\) angular integral encodes this sector in a rank--two Bessel kernel. The pure \(-A\) theory, exactly solvable in Cartesian variables, fixes the leading Bessel/HCIZ structure: its exponential selects alignment, while its prefactor removes the spurious doubled Wishart entropy. We then apply this structure to the transverse \(B\)-type expansion and its non-polynomial toy completion. Finite polynomial truncations lead to an apparent large--\(d\) perturbativity bound incompatible with the continuum limit, but this bound is shown to be an artifact of truncation. After summing the local transverse completion and balancing the compensating \(+A\) term, the Wishart saddle is recovered with the physical shifted mass. The resulting continuum behavior reproduces the universal \(-2d\) contribution of the \(D_\Lambda\)-channel, while the genuinely anisotropic \(\beta_\Lambda\)-channel lies outside the scope of a pure transverse \(B\)-type description. Finally, we outline the emergent Grassmannian geometry encoded by the two endpoint planes. Their relative angular fluctuations form a \(2(d-2)\)-dimensional sector, whose entropy interpretation is developed in the sequel. For \(d\ge4\), the two planes generically span a relational four-dimensional subspace of \(\mathbb R^d\).
item.dc:creator: Badis Ydri

item.title: Sparse anisotropic positive maps for qutrit entanglement: exact indecomposability and PPT geometry
item.description: arXiv:2607.12470v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Positive but not completely positive maps provide one of the most direct ways to detect entanglement beyond the positive-partial-transpose (PPT) criterion. We introduce and analyze an exactly solvable two-parameter family of sparse bistochastic positive maps on qutrits, in which two coherence channels are independently tuned by parameters $w$ and $z$. The sparse structure makes the full phase diagram analytic: positivity holds exactly on the square $0\le w,z\le2/3$, complete positivity on the smaller square $0\le w,z\le1/3$, and decomposability is lost precisely outside a quarter circle in the corner $w,z\ge1/3$. The indecomposable region is certified by explicit PPT entangled state adapted to the same witness geometry. At the endpoint $W_*=W(2/3,2/3)$ we construct a four-parameter family of PPT edge states of rank type $(5,5)$, derive their analytic detection region, and show that the corresponding rays are exposed faces of the PPT cone. Finally, although $W_*$ is not optimal, we give an explicit optimal refinement whose detection region on this family is strictly larger. The result is an analytically tractable qutrit setting in which positivity, indecomposability, PPT entanglement, optimality, and exposed convex geometry can be studied in a single framework.
item.dc:creator: Massimiliano F. Sacchi

item.title: Non-symmetric vector dyson equations
item.description: arXiv:2607.16333v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We study the vector Dyson equation $$-\frac{1}{m(z)}=z\mathbf{1}-\mathbf{a}+Sm(z),$$ with parameter $z$ in the complex upper half-plane $\mathbb{C}_+$, where $\mathbf{a}\in\mathbb R^d$ and $S$ is a nonnegative matrix, not necessarily symmetric. This equation has a unique vector solution $m(z)\in\mathbb{C}_+^d$, for which we establish a complete measure decomposition and prove regularity. We then develop a graph-theoretic approach to the singularity and stability problem for non-symmetric matrices $S$. The graph structure of $S$ identifies the possible degeneracies of the stability operator as $z$ approaches the real axis. In particular, for non-backtracking matrices, we prove square-root growth at regular edges, cubic-root growth at regular cusps, and complete stability estimates. We also obtain the corresponding estimates for symmetric matrices in the periodic setting.
item.dc:creator: Jiaoyang Huang, Zhonggen Su, Ruizhe Xu

item.title: Coherent-State Kernels for Composite Quantum Operations
item.description: arXiv:2607.23240v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: This paper develops a unified kernel-based method for computing exact matrix elements of composite quantum operations by inserting resolutions of the identity after individual operators or between successive factors of an operator chain. A single insertion gives an exact scalar identity, and nested insertions between the factors give multiple integral identities for chains of closed operators under explicit Bochner-integrability conditions. The procedure is carried through on polynomial and analytic functions of the ladder operators, on one- and two-mode Gaussian unitaries, and on three composite operations: a Kerr phase followed by squeezing or by a cubic phase gate, a two-mode squeezer followed by a beam splitter, and a heralded cat-state circuit with two beam splitters. At rational Kerr phases the Kerr-squeezed amplitudes reduce to finite sums of squeezed coherent-state amplitudes weighted by quadratic Gauss sums, with an explicit error bound at the remaining phases; the two-mode network gives a bivariate Hermite polynomial; and the heralded circuit gives closed forms for the amplitudes, the heralding probabilities and their extension to an arbitrary passive network fed by one squeezed source. The examples are set against the reach of four established techniques: operator ordering, the Berezin symbol calculus, Lie disentangling and the symplectic formalism. Each technique reaches a subset of the examples directly, while the insertion procedure reaches all of them under the same hypotheses. A comparison with direct Fock summation identifies the regime in which the finite Kerr sums are efficient, and the choice of resolution at each boundary of a chain follows a selection rule set by the action of the adjacent factor. Each closed form agrees with an independent numerical computation.
item.dc:creator: Ghasem Asadi Cordshooli

item.title: Optimality of Gaussian Entanglement of Formation
item.description: arXiv:2608.01909v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We prove that the entanglement of formation of every two-mode Gaussian state coincides with its Gaussian restriction, solving a longstanding open problem in continuous variable quantum information theory. The key result is a sharp affine relation between entanglement and a generalized Einstein--Podolsky--Rosen observable, valid for arbitrary pure two-mode states, including non-Gaussian ones. We further prove that the entanglement of formation is additive on arbitrary tensor products of two-mode Gaussian states, and hence coincides with the entanglement cost, settling the latter for all two-mode Gaussian states. As a consequence, we obtain in closed form the entanglement cost of thermal-loss, thermal-amplifier and additive-noise bosonic channels. Our results, which also extend to bisymmetric multimode states, establish that no two-mode state is less entangled than the Gaussian state with the same covariance matrix, yielding measurable lower bounds on both the entanglement of formation and the entanglement cost of arbitrary non-Gaussian states.
item.dc:creator: Gerardo Adesso

item.title: A priori error estimator for reduced-order models based on the higher-order Craig-Bampton method in dynamic substructuring
item.description: arXiv:2608.05625v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: The higher-order Craig-Bampton (HCB) method improves reduced-model accuracy through successive residual-mode enrichments. This study proposes an a priori estimator for the eigenvalue error remaining in the first-order HCB model (HCB-1) without using the full-order eigensolution. The estimator is defined as the relative difference between the HCB-1 and HCB-2 eigenvalues. Under symmetric Ritz approximation assumptions, ordered positive eigenvalues, nested augmented spaces, and preservation of retained eigenvalues by the System Equivalent Reduction Expansion Process (SEREP), the estimator is shown to be non-negative and to provide a lower bound on the relative HCB-1 eigenvalue error. A projection-based expression and an exact error identity are also derived, clarifying the conditions under which the estimator is accurate and showing that the lower-bound property alone does not guarantee a prescribed tolerance. Numerical results for a plate, an elbow pipe, and a reactor pressure vessel show estimation-to-error ratios of about 0.85-0.99, while a cost assessment reports the additional expense associated with the HCB-2 reference solution.
item.dc:creator: Jaemin Kim, Seung-Hwan Boo

item.title: Unique continuation at infinity for potentials with arbitrary radial growth
item.description: arXiv:2608.07276v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Let $G$ be any given continuous positive function on $\mathbb{R}_+$. Let $V$ be radial with $|V(x)|\leq G(|x|)$. We prove a Landis-type theorem for any real-valued solution of $\Delta u=Vu$ on $\mathbb{R}^n$. We construct a decay threshold $e^{-g(r)}$, where $g$ is a strictly increasing function which can be computed explicitly in terms of $G$. Under suitable assumptions the exponent in the decay threshold is proportional to the Agmon distance associated with $G$.
item.dc:creator: Henrik Ueberschaer

item.title: Arbitrarily Fast Quantum Dispersion in Long-Range Crystals
item.description: arXiv:2608.27326v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We construct the first examples of one-dimensional long-range crystals exhibiting arbitrarily fast polynomial dispersive bounds. The Floquet functions of our Hamiltonians are highly oscillatory Weierstrass functions, whose rough autosimilar structure drives the fast dispersion. The proof develops a new Fourier decay theory for $C^\alpha$ images of the Lebesgue measure, based on a Dolgopyat-inspired transfer operator method, and yields a van der Corput lemma for Weierstrass functions. As a consequence, the local time of classical Weierstrass functions of sufficiently large lacunarity exists and is $C^k$, answering a question raised by Geman and Horowitz in 1980.
item.dc:creator: Ga\'etan Leclerc, Mostafa Sabri, Tuomas Sahlsten

item.title: Protected domains and cooperative invasion on weighted networks
item.description: arXiv:2609.10463v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Reciprocal contacts can favor cooperation by protecting a lineage until its descendants compete as a group. An individual is chosen to reproduce from the whole population, with a probability increasing with its averaged cooperation payoff. Its offspring replaces a neighbor through contacts weighted equally in both directions. We compare a single cooperator taking over defectors with the reverse invasion, using the same distribution of introduction sites. When payoffs weakly affect reproduction, every network with at least six sites and a path visiting them all admits weights favoring cooperation at any benefit-cost ratio $b/c>1$. This holds for mutants placed uniformly or arising in newborn offspring. Unequal contacts sustain aligned domains around two protected sites, converting individual reproduction into collective competition. Cooperation cannot have an advantage when its benefit does not exceed its cost, at any positive selection strength with positive reproduction rates. Where mutants arise changes which contact patterns can use this mechanism. On a five-site path, the weak-selection threshold has the sharp lower bound seven under uniform placement; newborn introduction never favors cooperation at this order. We classify the contact patterns with at most five sites that can favor cooperation under either rule; newborn introduction requires a four- or five-site cycle. Tracing copies backward to their ancestors separates domain competition from the probability of reaching it. Exact polynomial inequalities prove sharp threshold bounds for paths and the four- and five-site cycles. The same ancestry reconstructs evolution without selection on weighted paths and cycles and fixes the slowest relaxation rate on every connected reciprocal network. Cooperation thus depends on both the collective competitors created by contacts and the route by which a new lineage enters them.
item.dc:creator: Abhishek Chowdhury

item.title: On Lorentzian Lie groups of Nonzero Constant Curvature
item.description: arXiv:2609.40017v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We investigate Lie groups endowed with left-invariant Lorentzian metrics of nonzero constant sectional curvature. We first revisit Heintze's theory and obtain a characterization of the Lie algebras of Riemannian Lie groups of negative constant curvature. We also extend classical results of Nomizu and Barnet to the pseudo-Riemannian setting by constructing a large family of Lie groups carrying incomplete left-invariant metrics of constant sectional curvature. We then describe Lorentzian Lie algebras of nonzero constant curvature according to the causal nature of their center and derived ideal. This description is complete except when the derived ideal is Lorentzian, for which we obtain a complete classification in dimension four. We show that every left-invariant Lorentzian metric of nonzero constant curvature on \(\mathrm{SL}(2,\mathbb R)\) is bi-invariant and complete. Moreover, a semisimple Lie group admits a complete left-invariant Lorentzian metric of nonzero constant curvature if and only if it is locally isomorphic to \(\mathrm{SL}(2,\mathbb R)\). We also characterize \(\mathrm{SL}(2,\mathbb R)\) through the existence of a noncentral spacelike left-invariant Killing vector field. Finally, we classify Lorentzian Lie algebras of nonzero constant curvature in dimensions at most four.
item.dc:creator: Mohamed Boucetta

item.title: An Algorithm for Generating All Berglund-Hubsch-Type Calabi-Yau Orbifolds and Their Mirrors. Classification of Maximal Admissible Groups
item.description: arXiv:2610.01957v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: In this paper, we present an algorithm for constructing all Calabi-Yau orbifolds and their mirror pairs associated with an arbitrary Berglund-Hubsch-type model, and prove its correctness. In particular, the proposed method yields explicit generators for the groups defining the corresponding orbifolds. The method for classifying maximal admissible groups is proposed. We illustrate the application of the classification approach to an arbitrary Fermat-type Calabi-Yau manifold. In addition, as an illustrative example, we classify all maximal admissible groups of Fermat-type Calabi-Yau threefolds.
item.dc:creator: Sergei Aleshin

item.title: On connection between associators and 6j-symbols
item.description: arXiv:2610.08044v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We propose a new formula relating the rationalized Drinfeld associators obtained from the Knizhnik--Zamolodchikov equation to the quantum $6j$-symbols of the algebra $\mathcal{U}_q(\mathfrak{g})$: $ U_{q} = U \cdot \Phi^{KZ}_{\mathbb{Q}} $. We prove this relation in the case of the $\mathfrak{sl}_N$ Lie algebra for the tensor cube of the fundamental and the first symmetric representation. We also check it perturbatively for the $\mathfrak{sl}_N$ algebra for representations $[2]\otimes [1] \otimes [1]$, $[2]\otimes [2] \otimes [1]$, the non-trivial cases with multiplicities --- $[2,1]^{\otimes 3}$, $[2,2]^{\otimes 3}$, and in the case of the $\mathfrak{so}_5$ Lie algebra for the tensor cube of the fundamental representation.
item.dc:creator: Elena Lanina, Artem Novokhatnii, Alexey Sleptsov, Radomir Stepanov

item.title: The three- and four-loop equal-mass sunset integrals and local Calabi--Yau fourfolds and fivefolds
item.description: arXiv:2610.10821v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We determine the equal-mass two-dimensional three- and four-loop sunset Feynman integrals $I^{(3)}_\circleddash$ and $I^{(4)}_\circleddash$ at large Euclidean momentum in terms of the genus-zero Gromov--Witten theory of the local Calabi--Yau fourfold and fivefold $X_L=\operatorname{Tot}(K_{F_L})$, where $F_L\subset(\mathbb P^1)^{L+1}$, $L=3,4$, is a smooth hypersurface of multidegree $(1,\ldots,1)$. At two loops the sunset integral is governed by the prepotential of a local Calabi--Yau threefold. For $L\geq3$ the moduli spaces of unmarked stable maps have positive virtual dimension and there is no prepotential, therefore the Feynman integral is governed instead by the one-point potential $\mathcal F_{\gamma_L}$ with insertion $\gamma_L=H^{L-1}/(L-1)!$, by its gravitational descendants, and by $\zeta(3)$ boundary terms coming from the Gamma class. At both loop orders the coefficient of $R^{L-1}$ in the Frobenius expansion in the mirror coordinate $R$ is $-\theta_Q\mathcal F_{\gamma_L}$ with the Novikov variable $Q=\exp(R)$. At three loops the whole Feynman integral is an explicit expression in $\mathcal F_{\gamma_3}$ alone, because genus-zero recursion determines all descendant series from it; at four loops two diagonal series suffice, and the $\zeta(3)$ term is itself corrected by $\theta_Q\mathcal F_{\gamma_4}$. At three loops we also derive the analytic normalization independently, from the Picard--Fuchs equation and the polar part of a Mellin transform, prove integrality of the multiple-cover transforms for arbitrary integral insertions together with an explicit quantum-$K$ formula, and compute the exact period connection polynomials. Finally we give endpoint values along the Euclidean axis, bounds on the Taylor radii in the Novikov variable $Q$, a computer-assisted proof of the four-loop endpoint nonanalyticity, and a comparison of the normalizations at two, three and four loops.
