item.dc:creator: Hartmut Maennel, Pierre Vanhove

item.title: Equal-mass sunset integrals and genus-zero local Gromov--Witten theory of Calabi--Yau $n$-folds
item.description: arXiv:2610.10828v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We prove an exact identity, as convergent logarithmic germs at large Euclidean momentum, between the equal-mass two-dimensional $(n-1)$-loop sunset Feynman integral, with $n\geq4$, and the genus-zero one-point descendant invariants of the local Calabi--Yau $n$-fold $X_n=\operatorname{Tot}(K_{F_n})$, where $F_n\subset(\mathbb P^1)^{n}$ is a smooth $(1,\ldots,1)$ hypersurface. Writing $s$ for the momentum variable and $y=-1/s$, the identity reads \[ I^{(n-1)}_{\circleddash}(s)=(-1)^{n-1}yA\,\Bigl[nR^{n-1}-\theta_Q{\mathcal D}_0^\Delta\,R^{n-2} +\sum_{j=0}^{n-3}c_jR^j\Bigr], \] where $R=\log y+O(y)$ is the local mirror coordinate, $A=\theta_yR$, $Q=e^R$, ${\mathcal D}_0^\Delta(Q)$ is the primary one-point potential, and each $c_j$ has the form \[ c_j=c_j^{(0)}+\sum_{a=0}^{n-2}\bigl(c_{j,a}\,{\mathcal D}_a^\Delta(Q) +c'_{j,a}\,\theta_Q{\mathcal D}_a^\Delta(Q)\bigr) \] with the coefficients in $\mathbb Q[\zeta(3),\zeta(5),\ldots]$ the odd zeta values coming from the Gamma class. The descendant series ${\mathcal D}_a^\Delta(Q)$ are given explicitly by the ambient hypergeometric series and the inverse mirror map. We also prove global univalence of the principal mirror map, with explicit upper and lower bounds on the $Q$-Taylor radii, extract the full primary evaluation divisor and its integral cover transform, and reduce the ambient endpoint constants to a finite universal Gamma-class part and $\lfloor(n-1)/2\rfloor$ real parameters.
item.dc:creator: Hartmut Maennel, Pierre Vanhove

item.title: Einstein-Cartan and Palatini-Cartan Gravity from Graded Poisson Geometry
item.description: arXiv:2610.11844v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Using notions from graded Poisson geometry, we develop a framework that allows for concise formulations of field theories such as Einstein-Cartan and Palatini-Cartan gravity. We show that Einstein-Cartan gravity is equivalent to a variant of Palatini-Cartan gravity in which the vielbein fields are constrained to satisfy appropriate symmetry relations, which we refer to as constrained vielbein gravity. To that end, we relate these theories via a diffeomorphism of graded manifolds. We then show how to obtain the full Palatini-Cartan theory by removing the symmetry constraint. Finally, we show how our graded geometric framework allows for a direct incorporation of the minimal BV extension of the graded constrained vielbein and Palatini-Cartan theories.
item.dc:creator: Johannes Moerland, Peter Schupp

item.title: Fiber product of condensable algebras and critical points of boundary phase transitions
item.description: arXiv:2610.12079v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: In this work, we propose a mathematical description of the critical point of boundary phase transitions in 2+1D topological orders. Given two boundary phases, $\mathcal{C}_A$ and $\mathcal{C}_B$, with corresponding Lagrangian algebras $A$ and $B$ in a 2+1D topological order $\mathcal{C}$, respectively, we propose that the critical point of the phase transition between these two phases, if it exists, corresponds to $D = A \times_{M} B$, which is the fiber product of $A$ and $B$ over $A$-$B$-algebra $M$. We prove that $D$ is also a condensable algebra. Additionally, we present an alternative classification of condensable algebras in $Z(Vec_G^\omega)$ and reveal splitting phenomenon that arises during the condensation of certain algebras. We also perform explicit computations for the condensable algebras within several examples of $Z(Vec_G^\omega)$, covering both Abelian and non-Abelian groups $G$.
item.dc:creator: Hanlin Lin, Hao Zheng

item.title: Plane wave representations for wave scattering on a sphere
item.description: arXiv:2610.15121v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Motivated by three-dimensional wave diffraction by conical shapes, we consider the two-dimensional problem of wave scattering on the real sphere $\mathcal{S}^2$ resulting from a point-source incidence on a scatterer $\mathbb{S}$. Using the recently introduced notion of plane waves on $\mathcal{S}^2$ as well as recent results on the Laplace--Beltrami Green's function $G$ on $\mathcal{S}^2$, we derive three plane-wave representations for the scattered field $u$. We then explain how $u$ can be analytically continued to the complexified sphere $\mathcal{S}^2_{\mathbb{c}}$. This allows us to formulate a complexified version of Green's third identity, and to provide a characterisation of complex sources. All our results are then used to draw strong analogies between planar and spherical scattering problems, notably through the introduction of directivities.
item.dc:creator: Valentin D. Kunz, Andrey V. Shanin, Raphael C. Assier

item.title: On the coincidence of discrete and continuous definitions of Entanglement of Formation
item.description: arXiv:2610.18816v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: It is proved that every Borel ensemble of pure states on a separable bipartite Hilbert space with finite average entanglement admits a countable ensemble with the same barycenter and arbitrarily small additional average entanglement. Consequently, the discrete and continuous versions of the Entanglement of Formation coincide on the whole space of states of infinite-dimensional bipartite quantum system (with infinite values allowed). The main idea of the proof (realized with the AI-assistance) is the lifting a Borel ensemble of pure bipartite states to a Borel probability measure on the unit sphere in the space of Hilbert--Schmidt operators followed by dividing the support of this measure into appropriate cells and replacing each cell by its conditional barycenter. The resulting countable ensemble is obtained by a recursive construction.
item.dc:creator: Haobo Ma, Maksim E. Shirokov, Wenlin Zhang

item.title: Exact analytical spectra of an effective field-modified radial Schr\"odinger equation by the Nikiforov--Uvarov method
item.description: arXiv:2610.20159v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We revisit the effective radial Schr\"odinger equation for a charged spinless particle in collinear static electric and magnetic fields that was formulated in our earlier work within the tridiagonal representation approach (TRA). In that model the angular factor of the electric coupling is replaced by the orientation parameter $C=\cos\theta$, the linear Zeeman term is diagonal in the azimuthal quantum number, and the effective field-modified central potential takes the form $V(r)=\Vt(r)+qECr$. Here we show that the same equation can be solved exactly without the TRA, by the Nikiforov--Uvarov (NU) method, once the potential component $\Vt(r)$ is prescribed. Three examples are worked out in closed form: a Kratzer-type component, which yields a linear-plus-Coulomb-plus-inverse-square central potential; a pseudoharmonic-type component, which yields a linear-plus-harmonic-plus-inverse-square potential; and a Hulth\'en-type component with a repulsive core (Manning--Rosen form), which yields a screened confining potential with a finite number of $s$-wave bound states. For each case we obtain the energy spectrum, the normalized eigenfunctions in terms of Laguerre or Jacobi polynomials, the location of the potential minimum, and closed-form radial moments. The spectra are independent of the orientation $\theta$ and of the electric field, in agreement with the structure found by the TRA, while the field enters through the shape of $V(r)$, the radial moments, and the expectation value $\langle V\rangle_k$. All analytical results are confirmed by an independent finite-difference diagonalization.
item.dc:creator: Tunde Joseph Osunmusanmi, Berihu Teklu
